# Plan: Juice & Atmosphere Pass (particles · night sky · weather)

## Context

The game is a complete survival sandbox (mining, 7-tier gear, farming, breeding, cooking,
beds, caves, ores, mobs, day/night) but feels **static**: there are **no particles** (no
break/death/splash/dust), **no night sky** (no stars/moon/clouds — just a flat sky-color
lerp and an invisible sun), and **no weather**. The user picked a "juice & atmosphere" pass
as the next step — the highest-ROI, lowest-risk follow-on to the merged UI polish, because
it's **pure procedural rendering/audio** with **no save-format and no worldgen impact**.

Outcome: breaking blocks throws colored shards, mobs puff on death, footfalls kick dust;
nights show stars, a moon, and drifting clouds; and it periodically rains/snows with
precipitation, an overcast sky, and a synthesized rain bed — all generated from code (zero
new assets), all transient/session-only.

## Architecture seams (verified against real code)

- **Event drain** `useMinecraftGame.ts:213-233` already calls `audio.handleEvent(event)` and
  `renderer.triggerSwing()` — add **`renderer.handleEvent(event)`** here.
- **Renderer** `GameRenderer.sync(state, timeMs)` runs every frame and ends in
  `syncDayNight(state)`; sub-views are factories (`createMobVisuals(scene)` etc.) returning
  `{sync/update, dispose}`, all freed in `dispose()`. New sub-views follow this pattern.
- **Positioned events**: `blockBroken`/`blockPlaced` emit in `mining.ts:93/124` (cell coords in
  scope); `mobDied` in `GameEngine.ts:372` (`mob.position` in scope). Add `x,y,z` additively.
- **Engine step order** `GameEngine.ts:185-190` — slot `tickWeather` right after `tickDayNight`.
  `weather.ts` is modeled on `systems/dayNight.ts`.
- **Audio** `audioDirector.ts`: `createDefaultGraph()` builds the AudioContext + gains;
  `sync(state, dt)` drives continuous sound; both early-return when `graph` is null.
- `world.getBiome(x,z): BiomeId` (Plains/Desert/Ocean/Forest/Mountains) → rain vs snow.
- `BLOCK_COLORS` (`lib/world/blocks.ts:71`, float RGB) and per-mob body hex
  (`MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs[0]`, `mobs.ts`) give particle colors.

## Hard constraints

- **Zero binary assets**: particles/stars = `THREE.Points` with vertex colors + a procedural
  canvas sprite; clouds = a `CanvasTexture` noise plane (same trick as `lib/ui/chromeTiles.ts`);
  rain audio = synthesized filtered noise. No image/audio files.
- **No save-format change, no worldgen change.** Weather is transient — **not** added to
  `serialize()` or `GameSnapshot` (like `mobs`/`cameraMode`). Worldgen SHA-256 hash tests and
  the save round-trip e2e must stay untouched.
- Engine stays headless/DOM-free; `lib/game/engine/**` and pure helpers must not import Three.js.
- Each slice keeps `lint`/`typecheck`/`test` green and is independently shippable.

---

## Slice 1 — Particles

**`lib/game/render/particlePool.ts`** (pure, DOM-free, unit-tested) — structure-of-arrays pool,
`PARTICLE_CAP = 512`. `createParticlePool()`, `spawnParticle(pool, p)` (recycle slot 0 at cap),
`updateParticlePool(pool, dt)` (gravity + drag integrate, age, swap-remove expired; clamp dt ≤ 0.1s).
No `Math.random` inside (jitter supplied by caller → deterministic, testable).
**`particlePool.test.ts`** — fill/age/retire/cap-recycle/determinism.

**`lib/game/render/particleSystem.ts`** — `createParticleSystem(scene)` → `{emitBurst, update, dispose}`.
One `THREE.Points` (position+color attributes sized to cap) + `PointsMaterial{vertexColors,
transparent, depthWrite:false, sizeAttenuation, map: procedural soft sprite}`; `frustumCulled=false`,
`raycast=()=>{}`. `emitBurst(opts)` is the only `Math.random` site (velocity/life/color jitter).
`update(dtMs)` steps the pool and uploads `count` particles via `setDrawRange`. Dispose geometry/
material/texture.

**Event enrichment (additive)** `state.ts`: add `x,y,z` to `blockBroken`/`blockPlaced`/`mobDied`
(existing tests assert only `type`+`blockId`/`kind`, so they still pass). Update the three emit
sites (`mining.ts:93/124`, `GameEngine.ts:372`).

**`GameRenderer`** — own `particles` (ctor + dispose); derive `dtMs` from a tracked `lastSyncMs`;
add **`handleEvent(event)`** mapping: `blockBroken`→~10 shards in the block's `BLOCK_COLORS`;
`blockPlaced`→small puff; `mobDied`→~14 puff in mob color; `ateFood`→crumbs at player; `jumped`/
`landed`→ground dust scaled by impact. `ateFood/jumped/landed` aren't positioned — read the
player foot/eye point tracked each `sync` (no event change for high-traffic motion events).
**Footstep dust** spawned in `sync` from a horizontal-travel cadence when on ground (model:
`audio/footsteps.ts`). Skip the pool step while `paused`.

**`useMinecraftGame.ts`** — add `renderer.handleEvent(event)` in the drain loop beside
`audio.handleEvent(event)`.

---

## Slice 2 — Night sky (stars · moon · sun disc · clouds)

**`lib/game/render/starField.ts`** — pure `generateStarPositions(count, seed): Float32Array`
(seeded hash like `chromeTiles.ts`; points on a sphere). **`starField.test.ts`** — determinism/shape.

**`lib/game/render/skyView.ts`** — `createSkyView(scene, camera)` → `{sync(state, timeMs), dispose}`,
all objects camera-following, `material.fog=false`, `raycast=()=>{}`, freed in dispose:
- **Stars**: `THREE.Points` (~800) at radius ~900, opacity `clamp01(1 - daylight*2.5)` (fade in at dusk).
- **Moon + sun disc**: small camera-facing sprites at `sunAngleAt(dayClock)` (sun) and the opposite
  angle (moon); sun fades by `daylight`, moon by `1-daylight`. (Sun currently has no visible body.)
- **Clouds**: large semi-transparent plane high above, `CanvasTexture` noise (Repeat wrap), drifting
  via `map.offset` over dt; follows camera x/z only.

**`GameRenderer`** — own `sky`; call `sky.sync(state, timeMs)` in `sync()` after `syncCamera`.

---

## Slice 3 — Weather (engine · renderer · audio) — cosmetic, transient

**`config.ts`** — `WEATHER_CYCLE_SECONDS = 180`, `WEATHER_RAIN_FRACTION = 0.35`.

**`lib/game/engine/systems/weather.ts`** (pure, DOM-free) —
`weatherAt(dayClock, seed): {active, intensity}` (seeded hash of the cycle index decides
precipitation; triangular envelope ramps intensity 0→1→0 — **pure on `dayClock`+`seed`, so the
substep catch-up loop can't desync it**). `tickWeather(state)` (no dt) sets `state.weather` and
picks snow (Mountains) / clear (Desert, Ocean) / rain (else) via `world.getBiome`.
**`weather.test.ts`** — determinism, intensity∈[0,1], biome→kind, rain-fraction sanity.

**`state.ts` / `GameEngine.ts`** — add `WeatherKind`/`WeatherState` and `weather: WeatherState` to
`GameState`; init `{kind:"clear", intensity:0}`; call `tickWeather(state)` after `tickDayNight`.
**Do NOT add `weather` to `serialize()` or `GameSnapshot`.** **Do NOT touch any spawn/daylight
threshold** — weather is cosmetic only (avoids balance/test churn).

**`lib/game/render/precipitation.ts`** — `createPrecipitation(scene)` → `{sync(state, dtMs,
cameraPos), dispose}`. Own pool + `THREE.Points` (rain = thin vertical streak sprite, fast
downward; snow = soft flake, slow drift). Target live count = `intensity * MAX` around the camera;
recycle particles that fall below/expire so the field follows the player. `clear`→ramp to 0.
**`GameRenderer.syncDayNight`** reads `state.weather`: lerp `liveSky` toward an overcast gray, pull
`fog.far` in, and dampen `sun`/`hemiLight` intensity by intensity.

**`lib/game/audio/rainLoop.ts`** — `createRainLoop(ctx, destination)` → `{setIntensity, dispose}`:
a looping white-noise `BufferSource` → lowpass → gain (synthesized, zero assets, off the SFX voice
budget). Add `rain` to `AudioGraph`, build it in `createDefaultGraph`, dispose it there; in
`audioDirector.sync` call `graph.rain.setIntensity(kind==="rain" ? intensity : 0)` (snow silent).
Add a no-op `rain` to the injected fake graph in `audioDirector.test.ts`. Optional rare thunder
one-shot (via injectable `rng`) at high intensity.

---

## Files

**New**: `lib/game/render/particlePool.ts` (+test), `particleSystem.ts`, `starField.ts` (+test),
`skyView.ts`, `precipitation.ts`; `lib/game/engine/systems/weather.ts` (+test);
`lib/game/audio/rainLoop.ts`.
**Edit**: `lib/game/engine/state.ts` (event coords, weather type+field), `systems/mining.ts`,
`engine/GameEngine.ts` (mobDied coords, weather init+step), `config.ts`,
`render/GameRenderer.ts` (own/dispose new views, `handleEvent`, dtMs, footstep dust, overcast),
`useMinecraftGame.ts` (drain wiring), `audio/audioDirector.ts` (rain loop), `audio/soundParams.ts`
(optional thunder), `audio/audioDirector.test.ts` (fake-graph `rain`).

## Verification

Per slice and final: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`,
`bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` (smoke) for the rendering slices.
- New unit tests: particle pool, star positions, weather system (all pure/deterministic).
- Confirm **`generation.test.ts`** (worldgen hashes) and **`save.test.ts`** + the save round-trip
  e2e (`smoke.e2e.ts:160`, `version===3`) still pass — proof of no save/worldgen impact.
- e2e: `renderedTriangles > 0` and the console-error fixture stay green (breaking a block now also
  emits a burst; night/weather add objects). Optionally assert triangles>0 with forced night/rain.
- Manual: break a block → shards; jump/land → dust; scrub to night → stars/moon/clouds; force rain
  → precipitation + overcast sky + rain bed; confirm pointer-lock/gameplay unaffected and FPS holds.

## Docs (same change)

`CHANGELOG.md` (one entry; note NO save/worldgen impact); `docs/architecture.md` (renderer
sub-views, audio rain loop, new `weather` system in the step order, weather is transient);
`AGENTS.md` "zero binary assets" stays true (all new visuals/audio procedural).

## Slice order & risks

Order: **1 Particles → 2 Night sky → 3 Weather** (each independently green). Risks & mitigations:
draw calls (one `THREE.Points` per system; caps 512/300; `depthWrite:false`, `raycast` no-op);
dt derived from tracked `lastSyncMs`, clamped ≤0.1s, frozen while paused; every new GPU resource
(incl. CanvasTextures) freed in `dispose()`; weather determinism guaranteed by `weatherAt` being
pure on `dayClock`/`seed`; audio degrades gracefully (rain loop lives in the graph, silent before
unlock / in headless tests).

# Plan: Juice & Atmosphere Pass (particles · night sky · weather)

## Context

The game is a complete survival sandbox (mining, 7-tier gear, farming, breeding, cooking,
beds, caves, ores, mobs, day/night) but feels **static**: there are **no particles** (no
break/death/splash/dust), **no night sky** (no stars/moon/clouds — just a flat sky-color
lerp and an invisible sun), and **no weather**. The user picked a "juice & atmosphere" pass
as the next step — the highest-ROI, lowest-risk follow-on to the merged UI polish, because
it's **pure procedural rendering/audio** with **no save-format and no worldgen impact**.

Outcome: breaking blocks throws colored shards, mobs puff on death, footfalls kick dust;
nights show stars, a moon, and drifting clouds; and it periodically rains/snows with
precipitation, an overcast sky, and a synthesized rain bed — all generated from code (zero
new assets), all transient/session-only.

## Architecture seams (verified against real code)

- **Event drain** `useMinecraftGame.ts:213-233` already calls `audio.handleEvent(event)` and
  `renderer.triggerSwing()` — add **`renderer.handleEvent(event)`** here.
- **Renderer** `GameRenderer.sync(state, timeMs)` runs every frame and ends in
  `syncDayNight(state)`; sub-views are factories (`createMobVisuals(scene)` etc.) returning
  `{sync/update, dispose}`, all freed in `dispose()`. New sub-views follow this pattern.
- **Positioned events**: `blockBroken`/`blockPlaced` emit in `mining.ts:93/124` (cell coords in
  scope); `mobDied` in `GameEngine.ts:372` (`mob.position` in scope). Add `x,y,z` additively.
- **Engine step order** `GameEngine.ts:185-190` — slot `tickWeather` right after `tickDayNight`.
  `weather.ts` is modeled on `systems/dayNight.ts`.
- **Audio** `audioDirector.ts`: `createDefaultGraph()` builds the AudioContext + gains;
  `sync(state, dt)` drives continuous sound; both early-return when `graph` is null.
- `world.getBiome(x,z): BiomeId` (Plains/Desert/Ocean/Forest/Mountains) → rain vs snow.
- `BLOCK_COLORS` (`lib/world/blocks.ts:71`, float RGB) and per-mob body hex
  (`MOB_TEMPLATES[kind].modelArgs[0]`, `mobs.ts`) give particle colors.

## Hard constraints

- **Zero binary assets**: particles/stars = `THREE.Points` with vertex colors + a procedural
  canvas sprite; clouds = a `CanvasTexture` noise plane (same trick as `lib/ui/chromeTiles.ts`);
  rain audio = synthesized filtered noise. No image/audio files.
- **No save-format change, no worldgen change.** Weather is transient — **not** added to
  `serialize()` or `GameSnapshot` (like `mobs`/`cameraMode`). Worldgen SHA-256 hash tests and
  the save round-trip e2e must stay untouched.
- Engine stays headless/DOM-free; `lib/game/engine/**` and pure helpers must not import Three.js.
- Each slice keeps `lint`/`typecheck`/`test` green and is independently shippable.

---

## Slice 1 — Particles

**`lib/game/render/particlePool.ts`** (pure, DOM-free, unit-tested) — structure-of-arrays pool,
`PARTICLE_CAP = 512`. `createParticlePool()`, `spawnParticle(pool, p)` (recycle slot 0 at cap),
`updateParticlePool(pool, dt)` (gravity + drag integrate, age, swap-remove expired; clamp dt ≤ 0.1s).
No `Math.random` inside (jitter supplied by caller → deterministic, testable).
**`particlePool.test.ts`** — fill/age/retire/cap-recycle/determinism.

**`lib/game/render/particleSystem.ts`** — `createParticleSystem(scene)` → `{emitBurst, update, dispose}`.
One `THREE.Points` (position+color attributes sized to cap) + `PointsMaterial{vertexColors,
transparent, depthWrite:false, sizeAttenuation, map: procedural soft sprite}`; `frustumCulled=false`,
`raycast=()=>{}`. `emitBurst(opts)` is the only `Math.random` site (velocity/life/color jitter).
`update(dtMs)` steps the pool and uploads `count` particles via `setDrawRange`. Dispose geometry/
material/texture.

**Event enrichment (additive)** `state.ts`: add `x,y,z` to `blockBroken`/`blockPlaced`/`mobDied`
(existing tests assert only `type`+`blockId`/`kind`, so they still pass). Update the three emit
sites (`mining.ts:93/124`, `GameEngine.ts:372`).

**`GameRenderer`** — own `particles` (ctor + dispose); derive `dtMs` from a tracked `lastSyncMs`;
add **`handleEvent(event)`** mapping: `blockBroken`→~10 shards in the block's `BLOCK_COLORS`;
`blockPlaced`→small puff; `mobDied`→~14 puff in mob color; `ateFood`→crumbs at player; `jumped`/
`landed`→ground dust scaled by impact. `ateFood/jumped/landed` aren't positioned — read the
player foot/eye point tracked each `sync` (no event change for high-traffic motion events).
**Footstep dust** spawned in `sync` from a horizontal-travel cadence when on ground (model:
`audio/footsteps.ts`). Skip the pool step while `paused`.

**`useMinecraftGame.ts`** — add `renderer.handleEvent(event)` in the drain loop beside
`audio.handleEvent(event)`.

---

## Slice 2 — Night sky (stars · moon · sun disc · clouds)

**`lib/game/render/starField.ts`** — pure `generateStarPositions(count, seed): Float32Array`
(seeded hash like `chromeTiles.ts`; points on a sphere). **`starField.test.ts`** — determinism/shape.

**`lib/game/render/skyView.ts`** — `createSkyView(scene, camera)` → `{sync(state, timeMs), dispose}`,
all objects camera-following, `material.fog=false`, `raycast=()=>{}`, freed in dispose:
- **Stars**: `THREE.Points` (~800) at radius ~900, opacity `clamp01(1 - daylight*2.5)` (fade in at dusk).
- **Moon + sun disc**: small camera-facing sprites at `sunAngleAt(dayClock)` (sun) and the opposite
  angle (moon); sun fades by `daylight`, moon by `1-daylight`. (Sun currently has no visible body.)
- **Clouds**: large semi-transparent plane high above, `CanvasTexture` noise (Repeat wrap), drifting
  via `map.offset` over dt; follows camera x/z only.

**`GameRenderer`** — own `sky`; call `sky.sync(state, timeMs)` in `sync()` after `syncCamera`.

---

## Slice 3 — Weather (engine · renderer · audio) — cosmetic, transient

**`config.ts`** — `WEATHER_CYCLE_SECONDS = 180`, `WEATHER_RAIN_FRACTION = 0.35`.

**`lib/game/engine/systems/weather.ts`** (pure, DOM-free) —
`weatherAt(dayClock, seed): {active, intensity}` (seeded hash of the cycle index decides
precipitation; triangular envelope ramps intensity 0→1→0 — **pure on `dayClock`+`seed`, so the
substep catch-up loop can't desync it**). `tickWeather(state)` (no dt) sets `state.weather` and
picks snow (Mountains) / clear (Desert, Ocean) / rain (else) via `world.getBiome`.
**`weather.test.ts`** — determinism, intensity∈[0,1], biome→kind, rain-fraction sanity.

**`state.ts` / `GameEngine.ts`** — add `WeatherKind`/`WeatherState` and `weather: WeatherState` to
`GameState`; init `{kind:"clear", intensity:0}`; call `tickWeather(state)` after `tickDayNight`.
**Do NOT add `weather` to `serialize()` or `GameSnapshot`.** **Do NOT touch any spawn/daylight
threshold** — weather is cosmetic only (avoids balance/test churn).

**`lib/game/render/precipitation.ts`** — `createPrecipitation(scene)` → `{sync(state, dtMs,
cameraPos), dispose}`. Own pool + `THREE.Points` (rain = thin vertical streak sprite, fast
downward; snow = soft flake, slow drift). Target live count = `intensity * MAX` around the camera;
recycle particles that fall below/expire so the field follows the player. `clear`→ramp to 0.
**`GameRenderer.syncDayNight`** reads `state.weather`: lerp `liveSky` toward an overcast gray, pull
`fog.far` in, and dampen `sun`/`hemiLight` intensity by intensity.

**`lib/game/audio/rainLoop.ts`** — `createRainLoop(ctx, destination)` → `{setIntensity, dispose}`:
a looping white-noise `BufferSource` → lowpass → gain (synthesized, zero assets, off the SFX voice
budget). Add `rain` to `AudioGraph`, build it in `createDefaultGraph`, dispose it there; in
`audioDirector.sync` call `graph.rain.setIntensity(kind==="rain" ? intensity : 0)` (snow silent).
Add a no-op `rain` to the injected fake graph in `audioDirector.test.ts`. Optional rare thunder
one-shot (via injectable `rng`) at high intensity.

---

**New**: `lib/game/render/particlePool.ts` (+test), `particleSystem.ts`, `starField.ts` (+test),
`skyView.ts`, `precipitation.ts`; `lib/game/engine/systems/weather.ts` (+test);
`lib/game/audio/rainLoop.ts`.
**Edit**: `lib/game/engine/state.ts` (event coords, weather type+field), `systems/mining.ts`,
`engine/GameEngine.ts` (mobDied coords, weather init+step), `config.ts`,
`render/GameRenderer.ts` (own/dispose new views, `handleEvent`, dtMs, footstep dust, overcast),
`useMinecraftGame.ts` (drain wiring), `audio/audioDirector.ts` (rain loop), `audio/soundParams.ts`
(optional thunder), `audio/audioDirector.test.ts` (fake-graph `rain`).

Per slice and final: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`,
`bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` (smoke) for the rendering slices.

sub-views, audio rain loop, new `weather` system in the step order, weather is transient);
`AGENTS.md` "zero binary assets" stays true (all new visuals/audio procedural).

## Slice order & risks

Order: **1 Particles → 2 Night sky → 3 Weather** (each independently green). Risks & mitigations:
draw calls (one `THREE.Points` per system; caps 512/300; `depthWrite:false`, `raycast` no-op);
dt derived from tracked `lastSyncMs`, clamped ≤0.1s, frozen while paused; every new GPU resource
(incl. CanvasTextures) freed in `dispose()`; weather determinism guaranteed by `weatherAt` being
pure on `dayClock`/`seed`; audio degrades gracefully (rain loop lives in the graph, silent before
unlock / in headless tests).

feat(render): procedural particle system for break/death/dust juice

The game had zero particles — mining, placing, kills, and footfalls gave no
visual feedback, which is a big part of why actions felt flat.

Add a pure, unit-tested structure-of-arrays particle pool (DOM-free, runs
under bun test) wrapped by a single THREE.Points draw call whose
position/color/size/alpha attributes refill from the pool each frame. A
small ShaderMaterial draws each particle as a soft round sprite that fades
over its life — no texture, so it stays a zero-asset effect.

The renderer now exposes handleEvent(event, state), wired into the event
drain alongside audio.handleEvent: blockBroken throws shards tinted from
BLOCK_COLORS, blockPlaced puffs, mobDied bursts in the mob's body color,
and ateFood/jumped/landed kick dust (landing scales with impact). Footstep
dust is spawned from a stride-distance accumulator in sync(); particles
freeze while paused. The three positioned events (blockBroken, blockPlaced,
mobDied) gain additive x,y,z fields so bursts land in the right place —
additive, so existing event assertions are unaffected.
EOF

13:AudioDirector (lib/game/audio/)  WebAudio: maps engine events + state → procedural sound
16:The engine has **no React, no DOM, no rendering** — it runs (and is tested) headlessly in `bun test`. The renderer, the audio director, and the input controller are the only modules touching Three.js scene objects, the `AudioContext`, and DOM listeners respectively.
18:## React shell (`lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`, `components/`)
20:- `useMinecraftGame` creates the `GameEngine` in the canvas mount's callback ref, then an effect builds the `GameRenderer`, the `AudioDirector`, and `inputController` and drives the `requestAnimationFrame` loop: `engine.step(dt, input)` (in bounded catch-up substeps of ≤50 ms, so slow frames — e.g. software GL — don't run the simulation in slow motion) → drain engine events (death/respawn handling, `attackSwung` → `renderer.triggerSwing()`, + `audio.handleEvent`) → `minimap.sync(state)` → `renderer.sync(state)` → `audio.sync(state, dt)` → `renderer.render()`. The minimap must sync **before** the renderer because it reads `state.worldMeshDirty`, which `renderer.sync` clears.
30:## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)
38:### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)
44:4. Player movement & physics (`systems/playerMotion.ts` — derives direction from `yaw`, scratch vectors, no per-frame allocations)
47:7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula)
48:8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
51:11. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)
55:## Renderer (`lib/game/render/`)
60:- `mobVisuals.ts` — mob id → model map; creates/removes models as mobs spawn/die and animates bob + leg gait from mob state (the simulation knows nothing about legs).
61:- `heldItem.ts` / `crackOverlay.ts` — first-person item model and the 8-stage mining crack box (stage = progress / hardness). Held blocks stay cubes; everything else is the item's 16×16 inventory sprite extruded into a pixel-thick voxel mesh (`extrudedSprite.ts`, vertex colors, silhouette-only side faces) — the render layer imports `lib/ui/spritePixels` for this, which is legal because spritePixels is pure pixel-buffer code with no DOM. The holder group is posed every frame by `heldItemPose.ts` (pure math): a one-shot swing on the `attackSwung` event (the shell calls `renderer.triggerSwing()` from the event drain), a looping swing while mining, a walk bob scaled by horizontal speed, an equip dip on slot switch, and a faint idle sway.
62:- `playerModel.ts` / `playerPose.ts` / `playerVisuals.ts` — the player's own humanoid body, visible only in third person: box meshes with pivot groups at the joints, walk gait + attack/mining chop from pure pose math (mirroring `heldItemPose.ts`), the look pitch applied to the head only, and the held hotbar item in the right hand via the shared `itemModel.ts` builder (also used by `heldItem.ts`).
66:## Audio (`lib/game/audio/`)
68:All sound is procedural — no audio files, mirroring the sprite system. SFX are synthesized by [ZZFX](https://github.com/KilledByAPixel/ZzFX) parameter arrays; music is a generative ambient pad over raw WebAudio nodes.
70:- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood). Music follows `state.daylight` immediately and the biome with 5 s hysteresis, and ducks while paused. The engine never imports this module.
71:- `synth.ts` — `SynthBackend`, **the only seam that touches WebAudio for SFX**: renders each `SoundDef` to an `AudioBuffer` once via `ZZFX.buildSamples` and plays it through gain/pan nodes with playback-rate jitter, a 10-voice cap, and per-sound retrigger throttling (which also de-dupes catch-up substep event bursts). Tests inject a recording fake instead.
74:- **Lazy unlock invariant**: no `AudioContext` exists until the first user gesture calls `unlock()` — including the `zzfx` import itself, which instantiates one at module scope and is therefore only ever imported dynamically inside `unlock()`. This satisfies the browser autoplay policy, keeps SSR/`bun test` import-safe, and keeps the console clean for the E2E fixture.
77:## Input (`lib/game/input/inputController.ts`)
83:## Inventory and items (`lib/game/`)
91:## World layer (`lib/world/`)
102:## Engine invariants & gotchas

- `heldItem.ts` / `crackOverlay.ts` — first-person item model and the 8-stage mining crack box (stage = progress / hardness). Held blocks stay cubes; everything else is the item's 16×16 inventory sprite extruded into a pixel-thick voxel mesh (`extrudedSprite.ts`, vertex colors, silhouette-only side faces) — the render layer imports `lib/ui/spritePixels` for this, which is legal because spritePixels is pure pixel-buffer code with no DOM. - `playerModel.ts` / `playerPose.ts` / `playerVisuals.ts` — the player's own humanoid body, visible only in third person: box meshes with pivot groups at the joints, walk gait + attack/mining chop from pure pose math (mirroring `heldItemPose.ts`), the look pitch applied to the head only, and the held hotbar item in the right hand via the shared `itemModel.ts` builder (also used by `heldItem.ts`).

-- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood). +- `audioDirector.ts` — the shell-side observer, exactly parallel to the renderer: `handleEvent(GameEvent)` plays one-shots (block break/place by material, hurt/eat/jump/land, mob attacks, death/respawn stingers) and `sync(state, dt)` drives everything continuous (footsteps, mining hit ticks, mob ambience, music mood, and the weather rain bed). Music follows `state.daylight` immediately and the biome with 5 s hysteresis, and ducks while paused. The rain bed (`rainLoop.ts`) is a looping filtered-noise source on the graph, off the SFX voice budget, whose gain tracks `state.weather` rain intensity (silent for snow / while paused). The engine never imports this module.

- `synth.ts` — `SynthBackend`, **the only seam that touches WebAudio for SFX**: renders each `SoundDef` to an `AudioBuffer` once via `ZZFX.buildSamples` and plays it through gain/pan nodes with playback-rate jitter, a 10-voice cap, and per-sound retrigger throttling (which also de-dupes catch-up substep event bursts). Tests inject a recording fake instead.

- `soundParams.ts` / `materials.ts` — pure data: ZZFX parameter tables per `MaterialGroup`/`MobKind` (tune by ear in the [ZZFX designer](https://killedbyapixel.github.io/ZzFX/)) and the exhaustive `BlockId → MaterialGroup` mapping.

- `footsteps.ts` / `mobAmbience.ts` / `musicBrain.ts` — pure schedulers/composer (distance-accumulator strides, per-mob randomized call timers with distance gain + look-relative stereo pan, pentatonic random-walk note generation). `musicPlayer.ts` renders notes as detuned pad voices through a lowpass and a procedural convolution reverb.

Makes the world react and breathe. Three additive layers, all **pure procedural rendering/audio** (zero new assets) with **no save-format and no worldgen impact**.

## What's new

- **Particles.** A pure, unit-tested structure-of-arrays pool (`particlePool.ts`) wrapped by a single `THREE.Points` draw call (`particleSystem.ts`); a small shader draws each particle as a soft round sprite that fades over its life (no texture). - **Night sky.** A deterministic 800-point star field that fades in at dusk, sprite discs for the moon and a now-visible sun on opposite ends of the sun arc, and a drifting cloud sheet from a seamlessly tiling canvas-noise mask (`starField.ts`, `skyView.ts`). Camera-following and fog-exempt; opacities ramp off `daylight`.
- **Weather.** A pure, deterministic system (`engine/systems/weather.ts`) sets a **transient** `state.weather` (never serialized) — time splits into windows, a seeded hash decides precipitation, biome picks snow (mountains) / clear (desert, ocean) / rain. 1	# Testing
2	
3	Two runners, three layers:
4	
5	- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
6	- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.
7	
8	## What is covered
9	
10	| Area                 | File                                                                                                                                  | What it pins down                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
11	| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
12	| Worldgen determinism | `lib/world/generation.test.ts`                                                                                                        | SHA-256 digests of generated worlds per seed (the save-compat contract), plus structural probes and meshing snapshots                                                                                                                                                                                       |
13	| Voxel store          | `lib/world/voxelWorld.test.ts`                                                                                                        | get/set/bounds/solidity and the voxel index formula saves depend on                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
14	| Raycast & collision  | `lib/world/queries.test.ts`                                                                                                           | DDA hit/previous cells and hit distance, AABB collision edges, water non-solidity                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
15	| Items & recipes      | `lib/game/config.test.ts`                                                                                                             | Referential integrity: every recipe/drop/armor mapping points at a real item                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
16	| Inventory algebra    | `lib/game/inventory.test.ts`                                                                                                          | Stack math, durability, crafting (including the refuse-on-full behavior), armor equip rules                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
17	| Save format          | `lib/game/save.test.ts`                                                                                                               | Round-trips, legacy-shape parsing, corrupt-data rejection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
18	| Simulation           | `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`                                                                                                  | Headless gameplay: boot, movement, hunger/regen gates, mining, commands (incl. pause/debug/camera-view/respawn), death/respawn, night spawning, save round-trips, gameplay event emission (block break/place, hurt, eat, jump/land, mob attack/hit)                                                         |
19	| Audio data           | `lib/game/audio/{materials,soundParams}.test.ts`                                                                                      | Every `BlockId` has a material group; every group/`MobKind` has well-formed ZZFX sound entries                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
20	| Audio schedulers     | `lib/game/audio/{footsteps,mobAmbience,musicBrain}.test.ts`                                                                           | Stride cadence and airborne reset; earshot gating, distance gain, look-relative pan, seeded call intervals; notes stay on scale, day/night/biome moods, deterministic under a seeded rng                                                                                                                    |
21	| Audio routing        | `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.test.ts`                                                                                                | With an injected fake `SynthBackend`: events → correct sound tables, staged mining ticks, footsteps while walking, pause ducking, mute/volume application                                                                                                                                                   |
22	| Audio settings       | `lib/game/audio/settings.test.ts`                                                                                                     | Round-trips, corrupt-data fallback, range clamping (own localStorage key, not the world save)                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
23	| Skin presets         | `lib/game/{playerSkins,skinSettings}.test.ts`                                                                                         | Preset integrity (six unique, valid colors, default-id fallback) and preference persistence (round-trip, corrupt/unknown-id fallback, swallowed write failures)                                                                                                                                             |
24	| UI sprites           | `lib/ui/*.test.ts`                                                                                                                    | Every item id renders a non-empty deterministic 16×16 sprite; HUD icon variants (full/half/container) differ; every skin preset renders a distinct bust portrait in its own palette                                                                                                                         |
25	| Minimap sampling     | `lib/game/render/minimapColors.test.ts`                                                                                               | Top-block detection (water visible), height shading, per-block colors                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
26	| Renderer logic       | `lib/game/render/{mobVisuals,heldItem,heldItemPose,extrudedSprite,itemModel,playerModel,playerPose,playerVisuals,cameraView}.test.ts` | Model lifecycle (create/reuse/remove/dispose), positioning, bob, item swaps, held-item swing/equip/bob poses, sprite-extrusion face culling and vertex colors, player-body gait/chop poses and visibility per camera mode, third-person camera placement (rear/front, clamped boom) — pure Three.js, no DOM |
27	| Components           | `components/game/*.test.tsx`                                                                                                          | InventoryPanel click-to-swap/equip/craft gating, Hotbar slots, StatusBars heart/hunger/armor meters, PauseMenu, DeathScreen (happy-dom + Testing Library)                                                                                                                                                   |
28	| Browser E2E          | `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts`                                                                                                                    | Real browser: boot without console errors, scene draws, input → movement, craft via UI, mining, camera view cycling, skin pick persisting across reload, pause freeze/resume, save via pause menu across reload                                                                                             |
29	
30	## Running the E2E suite
31	
32	```bash
33	bunx playwright install chromium   # once
34	bun run test:e2e                   # builds and starts the prod server itself
35	```
36	
37	E2E tests assert through `window.__monecraft` (the live engine/renderer/input handle — also handy in the browser console) instead of pixels; the one render check uses `renderer.renderedTriangles()`. The shared fixture fails any test that logs a console error.
38	
39	**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.
40	
41	**happy-dom has no `AudioContext`** (and the `zzfx` package instantiates one at import): everything above the `SynthBackend` seam is pure and tested with a recording fake (see `audioDirector.test.ts`); the WebAudio glue itself (`synth.ts`, `musicPlayer.ts`) plus real synthesis quality belong to the manual gameplay pass.
42	
43	**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.
44	
45	## The worldgen hash policy
46	
47	Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.
48	
49	**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**
50	
51	Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly two cases:
52	
53	1. A **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `SAVE_KEY` so old saves are discarded rather than corrupted.
54	2. A **Bun version bump** — the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined (ECMA-262 leaves transcendentals implementation-specific). CI pins `bun-version` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for this reason; bump both together and verify the digests merely shifted rather than the generation logic changing.
55	
56	To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values in the same commit as the cause.
57	
58	The same caveat means the hash tests prove _refactor purity on the pinned engine_, not cross-browser save portability — a player switching browsers may theoretically regenerate slightly different terrain for the same seed. That limitation predates the test suite; it is now at least documented.
59	
60	## Writing new tests
61	
62	- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
63	- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
64	- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
65	- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.

| Area                 | File                                                                                                                                  | What it pins down                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Worldgen determinism | `lib/world/generation.test.ts`                                                                                                        | SHA-256 digests of generated worlds per seed (the save-compat contract), plus structural probes and meshing snapshots                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Voxel store          | `lib/world/voxelWorld.test.ts`                                                                                                        | get/set/bounds/solidity and the voxel index formula saves depend on                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Raycast & collision  | `lib/world/queries.test.ts`                                                                                                           | DDA hit/previous cells and hit distance, AABB collision edges, water non-solidity                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Items & recipes      | `lib/game/config.test.ts`                                                                                                             | Referential integrity: every recipe/drop/armor mapping points at a real item                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Inventory algebra    | `lib/game/inventory.test.ts`                                                                                                          | Stack math, durability, crafting (including the refuse-on-full behavior), armor equip rules                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Save format          | `lib/game/save.test.ts`                                                                                                               | Round-trips, legacy-shape parsing, corrupt-data rejection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Simulation           | `lib/game/engine/GameEngine.test.ts`                                                                                                  | Headless gameplay: boot, movement, hunger/regen gates, mining, commands (incl. pause/debug/camera-view/respawn), death/respawn, night spawning, save round-trips, gameplay event emission (block break/place, hurt, eat, jump/land, mob attack/hit)                                                         |
| Audio data           | `lib/game/audio/{materials,soundParams}.test.ts`                                                                                      | Every `BlockId` has a material group; every group/`MobKind` has well-formed ZZFX sound entries                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Audio schedulers     | `lib/game/audio/{footsteps,mobAmbience,musicBrain}.test.ts`                                                                           | Stride cadence and airborne reset; earshot gating, distance gain, look-relative pan, seeded call intervals; notes stay on scale, day/night/biome moods, deterministic under a seeded rng                                                                                                                    |
| Audio routing        | `lib/game/audio/audioDirector.test.ts`                                                                                                | With an injected fake `SynthBackend`: events → correct sound tables, staged mining ticks, footsteps while walking, pause ducking, mute/volume application                                                                                                                                                   |
| Audio settings       | `lib/game/audio/settings.test.ts`                                                                                                     | Round-trips, corrupt-data fallback, range clamping (own localStorage key, not the world save)                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Skin presets         | `lib/game/{playerSkins,skinSettings}.test.ts`                                                                                         | Preset integrity (six unique, valid colors, default-id fallback) and preference persistence (round-trip, corrupt/unknown-id fallback, swallowed write failures)                                                                                                                                             |
| UI sprites           | `lib/ui/*.test.ts`                                                                                                                    | Every item id renders a non-empty deterministic 16×16 sprite; HUD icon variants (full/half/container) differ; every skin preset renders a distinct bust portrait in its own palette                                                                                                                         |
| Minimap sampling     | `lib/game/render/minimapColors.test.ts`                                                                                               | Top-block detection (water visible), height shading, per-block colors                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Renderer logic       | `lib/game/render/{mobVisuals,heldItem,heldItemPose,extrudedSprite,itemModel,playerModel,playerPose,playerVisuals,cameraView}.test.ts` | Model lifecycle (create/reuse/remove/dispose), positioning, bob, item swaps, held-item swing/equip/bob poses, sprite-extrusion face culling and vertex colors, player-body gait/chop poses and visibility per camera mode, third-person camera placement (rear/front, clamped boom) — pure Three.js, no DOM |
| Components           | `components/game/*.test.tsx`                                                                                                          | InventoryPanel click-to-swap/equip/craft gating, Hotbar slots, StatusBars heart/hunger/armor meters, PauseMenu, DeathScreen (happy-dom + Testing Library)                                                                                                                                                   |
| Browser E2E          | `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts`                                                                                                                    | Real browser: boot without console errors, scene draws, input → movement, craft via UI, mining, camera view cycling, skin pick persisting across reload, pause freeze/resume, save via pause menu across reload                                                                                             |

## Running the E2E suite

```bash
bunx playwright install chromium   # once
bun run test:e2e                   # builds and starts the prod server itself
```

E2E tests assert through `window.__monecraft` (the live engine/renderer/input handle — also handy in the browser console) instead of pixels; the one render check uses `renderer.renderedTriangles()`. The shared fixture fails any test that logs a console error.

**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.

**happy-dom has no `AudioContext`** (and the `zzfx` package instantiates one at import): everything above the `SynthBackend` seam is pure and tested with a recording fake (see `audioDirector.test.ts`); the WebAudio glue itself (`synth.ts`, `musicPlayer.ts`) plus real synthesis quality belong to the manual gameplay pass.

**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.

## The worldgen hash policy

Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.

**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**

Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly two cases:

1. A **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `SAVE_KEY` so old saves are discarded rather than corrupted.
2. A **Bun version bump** — the noise functions use `Math.sin`, whose exact results are engine-defined (ECMA-262 leaves transcendentals implementation-specific). CI pins `bun-version` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for this reason; bump both together and verify the digests merely shifted rather than the generation logic changing.

To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values in the same commit as the cause.

The same caveat means the hash tests prove _refactor purity on the pinned engine_, not cross-browser save portability — a player switching browsers may theoretically regenerate slightly different terrain for the same seed. That limitation predates the test suite; it is now at least documented.

## Writing new tests

- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.

18	`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.

21	`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
22	raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
23	above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
24	hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
25	changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.

36	eating. The two gates are the key feedback loop: you must stay above
37	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER` (12) to heal and above `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` (6) to sprint, so
38	hunger pressure indirectly throttles both combat recovery and escape speed. Keep
39	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER > SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` so there's a "can run but can't heal" band.
40

42

44	`HOSTILE_BURN_ABOVE_DAYLIGHT`, `HOSTILE_SPAWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `HOSTILE_CAP`.

47	`DAY_CYCLE_SECONDS` (240) sets the whole rhythm — a shorter day means more frequent

55

57	
58	`MINE_REACH`, `MINING_RATE`, `BARE_HAND_MINE_POWER`, `FIST_DAMAGE`, `ATTACK_REACH`,
59	`ATTACK_AIM_DOT`.
60	
61	Read by `systems/mining.ts` and `systems/combat.ts`. `MINING_RATE` × a tool's
62	`minePower` (from `items.ts`) ÷ block hardness = break time, so this constant scales

79	`CROP_GROWTH_CHANCE` probability — together ≈ 50 s/stage (~2.5 min to mature). More
80	samples or a larger radius means crops far from the player keep growing, at more
81	per-tick work. Breeding is bounded by `PASSIVE_CAP` (24) plus the crop cost of
82	feeding, so animals can't explode in number.

97

99

124	  pinned by hash tests — changing them requires the re-baseline policy in
125	  [testing.md](testing.md).

# Tuning & Balance

Every gameplay tunable lives in one place: [`lib/game/config.ts`](../lib/game/config.ts).
Each constant there carries a one-line comment; this guide is the companion that
groups them by **what they affect**, names the **system that reads each**, and
flags the **balance trade-offs** and the few that are **save-sensitive**.

To rebalance, edit `config.ts` — not the systems. Item-level numbers (a pickaxe's
power, a sword's damage, a food's hunger) are **not** here; they live with the
content in [`items.ts`](../lib/game/items.ts) (see the [reference](reference.md)).
Worldgen constants live in the frozen `GEN` object in
[`generation.ts`](../lib/world/generation.ts) and are pinned by hash tests — see
[testing.md](testing.md).

## Player feel — physics & movement

`GRAVITY`, `JUMP_VELOCITY`, `WALK_SPEED`, `SPRINT_SPEED`, `CROUCH_SPEED`,
`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.

Read by `systems/playerMotion.ts`. These set the moment-to-moment feel.
`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.

## Survival pressure — the main difficulty dial

`MAX_HEARTS`, `MAX_HUNGER`, `RESPAWN_SECONDS`, `HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`,
`WALK_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`, `JUMPS_PER_HUNGER`.

Read by `systems/playerStats.ts` (drain + regen) and `systems/playerLife.ts`
(respawn). This group is where "how hard is it to stay alive" is set. The
`*_PER_HUNGER` budgets control how fast activity drains food — lower numbers = more
eating. The two gates are the key feedback loop: you must stay above
`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER` (12) to heal and above `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` (6) to sprint, so
hunger pressure indirectly throttles both combat recovery and escape speed. Keep
`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER > SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` so there's a "can run but can't heal" band.

## Danger — day-night & the mob director

`DAY_CYCLE_SECONDS`, `HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`, `SPIDER_AGGRO_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`,
`HOSTILE_BURN_ABOVE_DAYLIGHT`, `HOSTILE_SPAWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `HOSTILE_CAP`.

Read by `systems/dayNight.ts`, `systems/spawnDirector.ts`, and `systems/mobAI.ts`.
`DAY_CYCLE_SECONDS` (240) sets the whole rhythm — a shorter day means more frequent
nights and more pressure. The three daylight thresholds are a **documented engine
invariant** (daylight ranges 0.04–1.0; see architecture.md): hostiles spawn below
0.28, spiders turn hostile below 0.42, and exposed hostiles burn above 0.72. Keep
them ordered `spawn ≤ spider_aggro` and `burn` well above both, or mobs will spawn
into instant sunlight. `HOSTILE_CAP` × `HOSTILE_SPAWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS` bounds how
crowded a night gets. Tests aim daylight explicitly (a `calmDaytime` helper) to
avoid first-night aggro.

## Progression — mining & combat reach

`MINE_REACH`, `MINING_RATE`, `BARE_HAND_MINE_POWER`, `FIST_DAMAGE`, `ATTACK_REACH`,
`ATTACK_AIM_DOT`.

Read by `systems/mining.ts` and `systems/combat.ts`. `MINING_RATE` × a tool's
`minePower` (from `items.ts`) ÷ block hardness = break time, so this constant scales
_all_ mining globally while item tiers scale it per-tool. Note the deliberate
asymmetry: `MINE_REACH` (7) is longer than `ATTACK_REACH` (4.5) — you can dig
farther than you can punch. `ATTACK_AIM_DOT` (0.89) is how precisely the crosshair
must point at a mob to hit it — lower is more forgiving. The per-ore **tool-tier
gate** itself lives in `systems/mining.ts` (`canMineBlock`), not config.

## Farming & breeding pace

Farming: `RANDOM_TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES`, `RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS`,
`CROP_GROWTH_CHANCE`, `GRASS_SEED_DROP_CHANCE`.
Breeding: `BREED_FED_WINDOW_SECONDS`, `BREED_PARTNER_RADIUS`,
`BREED_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `BABY_GROW_SECONDS`, `BABY_SCALE`, `PASSIVE_CAP`.

Read by `systems/randomTicks.ts` and `systems/breeding.ts`. The random-tick group
controls crop growth statistically: each interval samples `RANDOM_TICK_SAMPLES`
columns within `RANDOM_TICK_RADIUS` of the player and advances eligible crops with
`CROP_GROWTH_CHANCE` probability — together ≈ 50 s/stage (~2.5 min to mature). More
samples or a larger radius means crops far from the player keep growing, at more
per-tick work. Breeding is bounded by `PASSIVE_CAP` (24) plus the crop cost of
feeding, so animals can't explode in number.

## Beds & sleep

`SLEEP_ALLOWED_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`, `SLEEP_HOSTILE_RADIUS`, `SLEEP_FADE_SECONDS`,
`WAKE_DAY_PHASE`.

Read by the sleep path in `systems/interact.ts` / `GameEngine`. Sleeping is gated
to night (matching `HOSTILE_SPAWN_BELOW_DAYLIGHT`) and refused if a hostile is
within `SLEEP_HOSTILE_RADIUS`. `WAKE_DAY_PHASE` is where the day clock lands on
waking (a fresh dawn).

## Inventory

`HOTBAR_SLOTS`, `INVENTORY_SLOTS`, `MAX_STACK_SIZE`. **Save-sensitive** — see below.

## Persistence & rendering

`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS`, `SAVE_KEY`, `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`, `RENDER_RADIUS`,
`RENDER_GRID`, `THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE`, `THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN`.

`RENDER_RADIUS` is the biggest **performance** lever: the renderer meshes one region
of this radius around the player, so larger values draw more terrain at higher cost;
`RENDER_GRID` is how far the player moves before that mesh rebuilds (smaller = more
frequent rebuilds, fresher view). `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS` is how long an overlap is
tolerated before the auto-unstuck teleport fires.

## Save- and worldgen-sensitive tunables

Change these only with care:

- **`SAVE_KEY`** (`"minecraft_save_v5"`) is the localStorage key name. Note it's
  versioned independently of the save **schema** (currently v3, per
  [save-format.md](save-format.md)) — renaming `SAVE_KEY` orphans every existing
  player's save. Don't bump it to express a schema change; add a migration instead.
- **`INVENTORY_SLOTS` / `HOTBAR_SLOTS` / `MAX_STACK_SIZE`** affect the saved
  inventory layout. `save.ts` already migrates the v1 (40-slot) → v2 (36-slot)
  change; altering these again needs a matching migration or old saves break.
- **Daylight thresholds and `WAKE_DAY_PHASE`** shape the persisted `dayClock`'s
  meaning but are not save-format-breaking on their own.
- **Worldgen is not tuned here.** Terrain/ore/structure constants live in the
  frozen `GEN` object in `generation.ts` and are a byte-identical save contract
  pinned by hash tests — changing them requires the re-baseline policy in
  [testing.md](testing.md).
